newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia OTCs lead Singapore shares after Fed hike. [CORRECTED 10:32 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Malaysia OTCs lead Singapore shares after Fed hike. [CORRECTED 10:32 GMT]

text.p: Malaysian shares stole the limelight in the Singapore share market on Wednesday, returning in force after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised short term interest rates by 25 basis points.

The UOB OTC index measuring mostly Malysian over the counter stocks jumped 11.32 points to 1,300.96 and accounted for the bulk of the market's volume of 194.34 million shares. Advances led losers by 278 to 100 in the broad market.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index rose in the final minutes to end 11.65 points higher at 2,111.60 after spending most of the day in flat territory.
""Malaysian shares are making a comeback after the Fed hike," a dealer said, adding that the spread between Malaysian and U.S. rates was still quite wide and so there was no impact.
"I think Malaysian shares will be active in the next two weeks. Their share prices had fallen some 30 percent and now we'll see if they can break their previous highs," he added
Malaysia's MBf Land lead the actives with 8.6 million shares and rose Singapore $0.06 to S$1.15.
Labroy Marine (corrects from Pacific Andes) saw 2.24 million shares crossed at S$2.00. Fraser & Neave, Cycle & Carriage and Natsteel were firmer.
